correctness.rationale: Every cyclic section of an MEG set needs at least three vertices. The product-section criterion gives the lower bound 3n, and the balanced three-point-per-column floor mapping, via a proven cyclic index-gap bound and two verified exceptional matrices, attains it for every 5<=m<=n. Original edge-deletion distances were checked independently on 1422 torus edges; exhaustive cycle-gap equivalence checks cover 4064 cycle subsets. Finite tests are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The sharp sensor budget on every unequal rectangular toroidal grid is a motivated extension of the previously settled square problem. It closes a nonzero gap in known product bounds for all aspect ratios, supplies explicit optimal arrangements, and identifies two genuine small balanced-rounding exceptions. It addresses a canonical infinite graph-product family rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
